sections.title: The Coming of the Holy Spirit
observations: This section describes the dramatic event of Pentecost, where the Holy Spirit descends upon the apostles, fulfilling the promise made by Jesus before His ascension. The sound of a mighty rushing wind and the appearance of tongues of fire signify the powerful presence of God among His people.

The apostles begin to speak in different languages, which astonishes the crowd gathered in Jerusalem from various nations. This event marks the birth of the Church and the beginning of the fulfillment of the Great Commission.

sections.title: Peter's Sermon
observations: Peter stands up to address the crowd, explaining that the events they are witnessing are a fulfillment of the prophecy from Joel about the outpouring of the Spirit in the last days. He emphasizes that this is not drunkenness but a divine act of God.

Peter boldly proclaims the death and resurrection of Jesus, asserting that He is both Lord and Christ. He calls the people to repentance and faith, highlighting the necessity of turning away from sin and embracing the gospel.

sections.title: The Response of the People
observations: The crowd is cut to the heart by Peter's message and asks what they should do. Peter instructs them to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of their sins, promising the gift of the Holy Spirit to all who believe.

This section emphasizes the importance of community and fellowship among believers, as they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers. The early Church experiences growth and unity.

importantVerses.commentary: In the last days, God declares that He will pour out His Spirit on all flesh, indicating the inclusive nature of the gospel and the empowerment of all believers.
Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, highlighting the centrality of faith in Christ for salvation.
Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, emphasizing the response required for salvation and the importance of baptism.

questions: What does the outpouring of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost signify for the Church today?
How does Peter's sermon serve as a model for evangelism and preaching the gospel?
What role does baptism play in the process of salvation according to this chapter?
